1.title: AI, Machine Learning and Agentic AI Fundamentals
1.text: Welcome to Module six: A I, Machine Learning and Agentic A I Fundamentals. It covers the exam area three. Innovating with Google Cloud artificial intelligence. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. three point one Describe fundamental A I and M L concepts and how they create business value: define A I, M L, generative A I, data analytics and business intelligence. How agentic A I reshapes industries. The key benefits of Google Cloud's A I offerings. The business problems M L solves. Why data quality matters and its dimensions. Explainable and responsible A I. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three. Innovating with Google Cloud artificial intelligence (about eighteen percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: The vocabulary
1.text: The vocabulary. The figure shows this: A I contains machine learning, which contains generative A I; agentic A I builds on it.

1.title: The vocabulary, continued
1.text: The vocabulary. Artificial intelligence (A I). Systems that perform tasks that normally need human intelligence. Machine learning (M L). A part of A I where models learn patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules. Generative A I (gen A I). A I that creates new content: text, images, code, audio, video. Agentic A I. A I agents that reason, plan, use tools and take actions to reach a goal. Data analytics. Examining data to describe what happened and why. Business intelligence (B I). Reports and dashboards for decisions. A I and M L versus analytics and B I: analytics and B I explain the past and present with fixed queries and charts; M L predicts and classifies and gen A I creates; agents act. Exam tip: Analytics describes. M L predicts. Gen A I creates. Agentic A I acts.

1.title: How agentic AI reshapes work
1.text: How agentic A I reshapes work. Workforce productivity. Summarize meetings, draft documents, find company knowledge. Customer support. Resolve questions, route cases, hand over to people. Sales experiences. Personalize offers, prepare account research. Product innovation. Test ideas, generate designs and code. Operations. Automate routine workflows and approvals. Research. Search and synthesize large collections of material. Benefits of Google Cloud's A I offerings: best infrastructure for A I, an A I-ready data cloud, sophisticated first-party models (Gemini), an all-in-one A I developer platform and pre-built A I agents and applications.

1.title: Problems ML solves and its value
1.text: Problems M L solves and its value. Replace or simplify rule-based systems. A model learns the rules from data and adapts. Derive insight from large datasets. Find patterns humans would miss, in structured and unstructured data. Scale business decisions. Make millions of decisions consistently (credit, fraud, recommendations). Typical M L tasks: classification (spam or not), prediction (demand), recommendation, anomaly detection, vision, speech and language understanding.

1.title: Data quality
1.text: Data quality. A model is only as good as its data: garbage in, garbage out. Completeness. Is all the needed data present? Uniqueness. Are there no duplicates? Timeliness. Is the data recent enough? Validity. Does it follow the required format and rules? Accuracy. Is it correct? Consistency. Is it the same across systems?

1.title: Explainable and responsible AI
1.text: Explainable and responsible A I. Explainable A I. People can understand why a model gave a result, which builds trust and helps audits and regulation. Responsible A I. Fairness, safety, privacy, security and accountability; Google applies A I principles. Business implications. Reduces bias and legal risk, protects reputation, earns customer trust. Exam tip: Poor or biased data gives poor or biased results. Explainability builds trust, and trust enables adoption. Exam tip: Check the data first. If a model gives poor results, the exam answer is usually better, cleaner, more representative data, not a bigger model.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A marketing team wants to produce draft product descriptions and images automatically. Which technology fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Generative A I that creates new content. Generative A I creates new content such as text and images.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A customer support assistant plans several steps, uses company tools and resolves a request without a person. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Agentic A I that reasons and acts toward a goal. Agentic A I uses agents that reason, plan and act to reach a goal.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A lender replaces many hand-written credit rules with a model that learns from past loans. Which business value is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Replacing or simplifying rule-based systems. M L can learn patterns from data and replace complex hand-written rules.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A model trained on customer records performs badly because many records are duplicated. Which data quality dimension is the problem? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Uniqueness, since records are duplicated. Duplicate records are a uniqueness problem.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A regulator asks a bank why its model rejected a loan. Which concept helps the bank answer? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Explainable A I that shows why a result occurred. Explainable A I helps people understand why a model gave a result.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which statement best separates M L from business intelligence? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: M L learns patterns to predict while B I explains data with reports. B I reports on data with fixed queries; M L learns patterns to predict or classify.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does generative A I do? Answer: Creates new content. Question two. What is agentic A I? Answer: A I agents that reason, plan and act toward goals. Question three. Name three data quality dimensions. Answer: For example completeness, accuracy and timeliness.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does explainable A I provide? Answer: Understanding of why a model gave a result. Question five. Is M L part of A I? Answer: Yes, M L is a part of A I. Question six. Name one business problem M L solves. Answer: For example scaling business decisions.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Terms: A I contains M L, which contains gen A I; agentic A I acts; analytics and B I describe. Value: replace rules, find patterns, scale decisions. Data quality: completeness, uniqueness, timeliness, validity, accuracy, consistency. Responsible A I: explainable, fair, safe, private, accountable.
